name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention. '24x24' is a meaningful sprite dimension, not an address residue. 'dimmed_grayscale' accurately describes the hardcoded transform out = (src_byte & 7) + 0x18, which maps every painted pixel into the fixed 8-step grayscale palette band 0x18..0x1F. No address residue in the name.
purpose: Hand-written RLE blit of a 24x24 sprite, recolouring every painted pixel into the fixed 8-step grayscale band 0x18..0x1F (out = (src&7)+0x18) to render dimmed/inactive portraits and the already-acted-character battle sprite.
logic_summary: Iterates 24 rows; each row resets x_remain to 0x18 and decodes RLE command bytes until x_remain hits 0, then advances dst by stride-0x18. Command top 2 bits select mode, low 6 bits +1 = run length: 00=RUN (paint len grayscale pixels from one source byte, dst+=len), 01=STRIDE-2 RUN (paint at every other dst byte, dst+=2*len, x-=2*len), 10=LITERAL (one source byte per pixel, dst+=len), 11=TRANSPARENT SKIP (advance dst by len, no source consumed). The grayscale transform (src&7)+0x18 is applied in the RUN/STRIDE-2/LITERAL modes. This is the off=0/base=0x18 special case of fd2_tile_blit_24x24_with_tint_offset @ 0x4DC34 (identical RLE bodies). Leaf, no CHK, no CALLs.
signature: void __cdecl fd2_tile_blit_24x24_dimmed_grayscale(uint32 src, uint32 dst, uint32 stride)

params.name: src
params.semantics: Source RLE-encoded 24x24 sprite stream base address (assigned to rle_stream and decoded byte-by-byte). Callers pass a portrait/char sprite pointer resolved from the portrait_sprite_cache atlas.
params.reason: Accurately names the source stream; matches sibling blitters' param naming; no address residue.

params.name: dst
params.semantics: Destination base linear address (assigned to dst_buf); pixels written here, advancing per row by stride-0x18.
params.reason: Accurate; matches sibling blitters; no address residue.

params.name: stride
params.semantics: Destination row stride in bytes; row reset advances by stride-0x18. 0x1C8 from battle painter @ 0x127E0, 0x140 from recruitment screen @ 0x31E80.
params.reason: Accurate; matches sibling blitters; no address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value; output is the blitted sprite in dst.

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was thorough and correct, but characterized the battle-painter usage as the 'dead-character path'. Caller fd2_paint_char_sprite_at_world_pos @ 0x127E0 actually selects this blitter on the (bFlags & 0x80) != 0 = acted-this-turn branch (greyed-when-acted), not a death flag. Refined to 'already-acted-character path (bFlags & 0x80 = acted-this-turn branch)'.
notes: Verified both callers by decompilation: battle painter @ 0x127E0 uses this blitter on bFlags&0x80 (acted) branch with stride 0x1C8; recruitment @ 0x31E80 uses it for selection_state==0 (unselected) portraits with stride 0x140. Function body in src matches decompilation exactly including the STRIDE-2 x_remain -= 2*count. Refined only the 'dead-character' wording in both src comment and Ghidra plate to the precise 'already-acted-character / bFlags&0x80 acted-this-turn' characterization; all other comment content kept. No logic changes.
